meta.note: Curated index of AI providers that offer free or trial API access. Figures are transcribed from official docs on the verified date. Limits change without notice - always confirm in the provider console before relying on a quota.

providers.name: Groq
providers.summary: LPU-based inference with the most generous always-free tier for open models. Fastest time-to-first-token in the index.
providers.notes: Free limits are per model, not per account - gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-20b each get their own 30 RPM / 1K RPD bucket, so spreading load across models multiplies throughput. Whisper runs on a separate 20 RPM / 2K RPD allowance.

providers.name: OpenRouter
providers.summary: Single API in front of 300+ models. Any model ID ending in ':free' is zero-cost, with a per-minute and per-day cap.

limits.text: 50 RPD until you buy 10 credits, then 1,000 RPD

providers.notes: The daily ceiling is set by all-time credits purchased, not current balance - a one-off 10-credit top-up permanently raises free-model RPD from 50 to 1,000 (granted from 9 credits to absorb rounding). Creating extra accounts does not help; capacity is governed globally.

providers.name: Google Gemini API
providers.summary: Free tier keyed to a Google AI Studio project. Multimodal, long context, and the strongest free OCR/vision stack available at zero cost.

limits.text: Per-model RPM / TPM / RPD - see AI Studio rate-limit page (limits are no longer published in docs)

providers.regions: Global, excluding a few restricted territories
providers.notes: Policy tightened in October 2026: free-tier text access narrowed toward the Flash-Lite class, with Pro-class models moving behind billing. Limits are enforced per project rather than per key and RPD resets at midnight Pacific. Check the AI Studio rate-limit dashboard for your actual numbers.

providers.name: Cerebras Inference
providers.summary: Wafer-scale inference at extreme token throughput. No permanent free tier - the free trial is time-bounded credits.

limits.text: qwen-3.8-27b gets 15 RPM · 1M TPD · trial credits only

providers.notes: Verified as of October 2026: Cerebras explicitly states there is no permanently free tier. New accounts receive $5 in credits after adding a verified payment method, expiring 30 days after grant. Without a payment method, both Playground and API stay inactive.

providers.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
providers.summary: Serverless GPU inference billed in Neurons, with a daily free allocation that renews. Pairs naturally with Workers and Pages Functions.

limits.text: 10,000 Neurons per day free (resets daily)

providers.notes: Neurons are a blended unit covering text, image and audio models, so a single daily budget is shared across modalities. The account ID is part of the URL path; the OpenAI-compatible route needs it substituted.

providers.name: GitHub Models
providers.summary: Multi-vendor model catalog behind a GitHub personal access token. No separate signup, no card - useful when you already live in GitHub.

limits.text: Per-model request and token caps by GitHub plan tier - see rate-limit page for your account

providers.notes: Authentication uses a GitHub PAT rather than a vendor API key. Free-tier ceilings scale with your GitHub plan, so a Copilot Pro or Enterprise seat raises them. Intended for prototyping and evaluation, not production traffic.

providers.name: Mistral AI
providers.summary: European lab with a free experimentation tier on La Plateforme covering the small and medium model line-up.

limits.text: Free experimentation tier - 1 request/second class limits, token caps vary by model

providers.notes: The free tier is labelled for experimentation and excludes the flagship Large models. Phone verification is required on signup. Useful when you need an EU-domiciled provider for data-residency reasons.

providers.name: Hugging Face Inference Providers
providers.summary: Routes to a dozen inference backends through one token. Free accounts get a small monthly credit allowance that renews.

limits.text: Small monthly inference credit for free accounts, shared across all providers

providers.notes: The free credit is denominated in dollars, so expensive models burn it in a handful of calls while small models stretch much further. Enabling a PRO subscription raises the monthly allowance substantially.

providers.name: NVIDIA NIM
providers.summary: Hosted microservices for open models on NVIDIA infrastructure, with a credit grant on signup for build.nvidia.com.

limits.text: 1,000 API credits on signup for hosted endpoints

providers.notes: Credits are one-time, not recurring. The same model catalog can be self-hosted via NIM containers, which removes API cost entirely if you have GPU capacity.

providers.name: SambaNova Cloud
providers.summary: RDU-accelerated inference with a genuinely free developer tier and very high token throughput on open models.

limits.text: Free developer tier with per-model RPM and token caps - see cloud console

providers.notes: Free tier is rate-limited rather than credit-limited, which makes it better for steady low-volume use than for bursty batch jobs. Context ceilings are lower than the model names suggest.

providers.name: Cohere
providers.summary: Trial keys for Command and Embed models, aimed at evaluation. Strong at RAG-oriented embeddings and reranking.

limits.text: 1,000 calls per month on trial keys

providers.notes: Trial keys are capped at 1,000 calls per month in total, not per model, so a chatty pipeline exhausts them quickly. The API is not OpenAI-shaped - use the native SDK or the compatibility layer.

providers.name: Together AI
providers.summary: Broad open-weights catalog including image and audio models, with a signup credit for new accounts.

limits.text: One-time signup credit for new accounts - amount varies by promotion

providers.notes: Some models are flagged as serverless-free during preview windows and are usable without consuming credit. Credits are consumed by fine-tuning jobs as well as inference.

providers.name: Fireworks AI
providers.summary: Fast serving of open models with a small trial credit. Strong function-calling and structured-output support.

limits.text: Small one-time trial credit on signup

providers.notes: Model IDs require the full 'accounts/fireworks/models/...' prefix, which trips up generic OpenAI clients. Trial credit is small - enough for evaluation, not for a demo with real traffic.

providers.name: SiliconFlow
providers.summary: Chinese aggregator that keeps a rotating set of small and mid-size open models permanently free, with OpenAI-compatible routing.

limits.text: Free model tier with per-model RPM caps - check the model list for the free badge

providers.notes: Which models are free rotates over time, so hard-coding a free model ID will eventually break. Separate base URLs exist for the China and international regions - using the wrong one returns auth errors rather than a clear message.

providers.name: Zhipu AI (GLM)
providers.summary: GLM model family with a permanently free Flash-class text model and a generous entry quota for new accounts.

limits.text: Free tier on Flash models; concurrency-based caps rather than strict RPM

providers.notes: Rate limiting is expressed as concurrency (simultaneous requests) rather than requests per minute, which makes quota planning unintuitive. Global users should use the z.ai domain instead of the China endpoint.

providers.name: Alibaba Cloud Model Studio
providers.summary: Qwen family served through DashScope, with a free token allowance per model for new accounts and permanently free small models.

limits.text: Free token quota per model (varies by model and region); qwen-turbo class has a standing free allowance

providers.notes: The international and China regions are entirely separate: keys, quotas and base URLs do not cross over. The compatible-mode endpoint is the one to use with OpenAI SDKs.

providers.name: Moonshot AI (Kimi)
providers.summary: Long-context Kimi models with a signup credit grant on the open platform.

limits.text: One-time trial credit on registration - see console

providers.notes: Long-context requests are billed on the full prompt, so a 128K-token call can consume a trial credit in a single request. China and international platforms are separate accounts.

providers.name: ModelScope
providers.summary: Model hub with a free inference API for a rotating catalog of open models, including image generation.

limits.text: Free daily call quota per model (commonly ~2,000 calls/day) - see model page

providers.notes: Quota is granted per model, not per account, so several free models can be combined. Throughput is best-effort and queues during peak hours.

providers.name: Pollinations.AI
providers.summary: Keyless text and image generation over plain HTTP GET - no signup, no token, no SDK. The lowest-friction entry in this index.

limits.text: Anonymous tier is rate-limited per IP; a free token raises the ceiling

providers.notes: Because there is no key, the service is explicitly for demos and experiments - do not put it behind a production feature. Image generation works via a URL template, which makes it trivially embeddable in HTML.

providers.name: Ollama
providers.summary: One-command local model runtime with an OpenAI-compatible server. Unlimited requests, zero cost, full privacy.

limits.text: Unlimited - bounded only by your hardware

providers.notes: Set OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0 to reach it from containers or other machines; by default it binds to localhost only. The OpenAI compatibility layer covers chat completions and embeddings but not every upstream parameter.

providers.name: LM Studio
providers.summary: Desktop GUI for running GGUF and MLX models with a built-in OpenAI-compatible server and model browser.

limits.text: Unlimited - bounded only by your hardware

providers.notes: The local server is off by default - start it from the Developer tab. Free for personal and professional use, but the licence restricts commercial redistribution of the app itself.

providers.name: vLLM
providers.summary: High-throughput serving engine with PagedAttention. The standard choice for self-hosting open weights on your own GPUs.

limits.text: Unlimited - bounded by GPU capacity and your concurrency settings

providers.notes: Throughput depends heavily on --gpu-memory-utilization and --max-model-len; the defaults are conservative and leave GPU memory idle. Needs a CUDA or ROCm host, so it is not a laptop option.

providers.name: Hyperbolic
providers.summary: Decentralised GPU marketplace offering open-model inference with a small signup credit.

limits.text: Small one-time signup credit - see billing dashboard

providers.notes: Model availability shifts with GPU supply, so an endpoint that works today may be withdrawn. Credits do not expire quickly, which makes it a reasonable fallback account to keep dormant.

providers.name: Nebius AI Studio
providers.summary: European GPU cloud with an inference studio for open models and a signup credit.

limits.text: One-time trial credit on signup - see console

providers.notes: A sensible option when EU data residency matters and Mistral's free tier is too small. Token pricing on open models is among the lowest in the index once the credit runs out.

providers.name: Novita AI
providers.summary: Broad open-model catalog with aggressive pricing and a small trial balance for new accounts.

limits.text: Small one-time trial credit - see billing page

providers.notes: Note the '/v3/openai' path segment - the base URL differs from most OpenAI-compatible providers and is a common misconfiguration. Trial balance is consumed by image generation very quickly.
